name: Iceland

income_tax.summary: Three state brackets (16.55%, 23.05%, 31.35%) plus the 14.94% withholding municipal rate, giving 31.49%, 37.99% and 46.29% (PwC, 2026). The personal tax credit of ISK 72,492 a month (ISK 869,904 a year, Skatturinn) is modelled as a zero bracket of about ISK 2.76 million. Employee pension contribution 4%.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: PwC says the 15.5% minimum total pension contribution (4% employee share, deductible, + 11.5% employer share) applies to all employees' and self-employed persons' remunerations, so a self-employed person bears the full 15.5%. Flat fees: elderly fund ISK 14,614 and broadcasting contribution ISK 22,200. The social-insurance levy (tryggingagjald) on a self-employed person's imputed salary is not on the PwC page and was not checked, so it is not counted.
income_tax.local_tax_note: 14.94% is the maximum municipal rate used for withholding (12.44%-14.94% in the final assessment). The personal tax credit (ISK 72,492 a month, ISK 869,904 a year) is confirmed on Skatturinn's personal-tax-credit page and converted to an equivalent zero bracket (credit / 31.49% = ISK 2,762,432).

regimes.name: Long-term visa for remote workers
regimes.description: Visa for non-EEA citizens working remotely for foreign employers or clients, with proof of monthly income of ISK 1,000,000 (ISK 1,300,000 with a spouse). Stays of 90 to 180 days, not renewable; holders cannot work for Icelandic employers. No special tax treatment: ordinary rules apply, and a stay under 183 days normally does not create tax residence.
regimes.duration_note: Up to 180 days; must leave and reapply from outside Iceland.
